Justice Veena Birbal, President

 

 

 
 In this appeal, challenge is made to order dated 18.9.13 passed by the District Consumer Disputes Redessal Forum, ISBT, Kashmere Gate, Delhi (in short the "District Forum") in Complaint Case No. 739/2008 whereby the Ld. District Forum has directed the appellant/OP to pay the following amounts to the respondent/complainant:
"1.       To pay to the complainants a sum of Rs.61,360/- (Rs. Sixty One Thousand Three Hundred Sixty Only) as hotel accommodation charges.
To pay to the complainants a sum of Rs.70,000/- (Rs. Seventy Thousand) as compensation for causing harassment, pain and mental agony.
3.   To pay to the complainants a sum of Rs.10,000/-(Rs.Ten Thousand) as cost of litigation."
The facts relevant for the disposal of the appeal are as under:
The respondents herein were the complainants before the District Forum. Respondent No.1 is the Managing Director and respondent No.2 is the Director of M/s. Apex Encon Projects Pvt. Ltd. and are engaged in infrastructure business.  The respondents/complainants were invited by the SANDVIK to participate in the "BAUMA 2007 INTERNATIONAL EXHIBITION" in Munich, Germany during the period 23.04.2007 to 29.04.2007.   The respondents/complaints had taken tour package from appellant/OP from 22.04.2007 to 27.04.2007 which included return Economy Class Group Air Fare on Lufthansa or similar Airlines, accommodation on twin sharing basis, daily Buffet Breakfast for the said period, daily India Veg./Non-Veg. Buffet Dinner in the comfort of its hotel for the said period, pickup on 22nd April from Airport to Hotel, daily Pick and Drop from Hotel to Fair ground by Luxury AC coach, German Schnegen VISA Fee, Medi-Claim and documentation, Airport Taxes, courier communication charges, Gratuities to overseas service Provide, Attractive Nimble Travel Kit and services of Nimble's Tour Manager.  The total cost of tour was Rs.2,35,000/-, the respondent had paid Rs.2,25,000/- by way of cheque and demand draft on 14.04.2007 and 23.04.2007 respectively.  On 23.04.2007, the complainant informed the Tour Operator that room would not be required in the package as the rooms were arranged by the invitee of the respondents/complainants and asked for refund of room rent.  However, the appellant/OP informed that the rooms which had already been booked, no refund could be given and cancellation was not possible.  Accordingly, the respondent/complainant asked their invitee to use their rooms for someone else.  The grievance of the respondents/complainants was that without their consent, the appellant/OP had given their rooms to someone else during the period of contract with them.  It was also their case that they had informed the invitees of having made their own arrangement.  In all, following four deficiencies were alleged by the respondents/complainants on the part of the appellant/OP:
"1.       VISA not made by 20.04.2007 and, as such, departure for Munich could not take place on 22.04.2007.  VISA was received on 23.04.2007 and, as such, departure was possible only on 25.04.2007.
2.         Hotel accommodation was booked for 22.04.2007 to 27.04.2007 but was not made available.
3.         Facility of pickup from airport to hotel accommodation and from hotel to the place of venue was not arranged.
4.         Date of return of journey was not changed inspite of offer of making the payment as per agreements."
3. Alleging aforesaid deficiencies in service, the respondents/complainants had claimed refund of paid amount of Rs.2,25,000/- along with Rs.1 lac as compensation for causing inconvenience to them.  The respondents/complainants had also prayed for interest and litigation expenses.
4. The appellant/OP contested the complaint case by filing written statement before the Ld. District Forum wherein the allegations made against it were denied.  The appellant/OP had alleged that the VISA fee was included in the tour package and they had done everything on their part to make VISA available for respondents/complainants as per schedule time and there was no lack of service on their part.  About hotel accommodation also, the stand of the appellant/OP was that cancellation of room was done at the request of the respondents/complainants and appellant/OP had also agreed to forego Rs.10,000/-.  It was also alleged that the appellant/OP made efforts to get alternative hotel accommodation, however, the same could not be arranged.  It was alleged that there was no deficiency on their part.  About facility of pick up from airport and the hotel accommodation, their stand was that there was no such agreement in this regard.  The appellant/OP never agreed to provide for the same as the same was not part of tour package. The other allegations were also denied.
5. Both the parties had led evidence by way of affidavits.
6. After hearing the parties and considering the material on record, the Ld. District Forum found that there was no deficiency on the part of the appellant/OP as had been alleged at serial No.1, 3 & 4 above. However, as regards the booking of hotel accommodation, the Ld. District Forum held that the same was not made available to respondents/complainants and rather appellant/OP had got booked rooms for someone else.  It was  held that there was deficiency on the part of the appellant/OP and order has been made for the refund of hotel accommodation charges besides granting compensation and litigation expenses as has been stated above.
7. Aggrieved with the same, present appeal is filed.
8. Ld. Counsel for the appellant has contended that District Forum has erred in holding that the appellant/OP is liable to pay a sum of Rs.61,360/- to the respondents towards hotel accommodation as the appellant had agreed to provide for said service.  It is contended that the appellant had agreed to provide said service only on the assurance of payment of balance amount of Rs.10,000/-.  It is contended that rooms were cancelled at the request of the respondents/complainants and also that the appellant/OP did not charge balance amount of Rs.10,000/-.  It is contended that the accommodation was cancelled at the request of the respondent/complainant as such there was no deficiency on the part of the appellant.  It is contended that the relevant evidence has been ignored by the Ld. District Forum and appellant has been asked to pay Rs.70,000/- as compensation as well as refund of hotel accommodation without any fault on its part.
9.  We have heard the arguments and gone through the material on record.
10.  It is admitted position that the tour package along with other services was taken from the appellant/OP for the period from 22.4.07 to 27.4.07 as the respondents/complainants had to participate in "BAUMA 2007 INTERNATIONAL EXHIBITION" in Munich, Germany.
11.  It is also admitted position that on 3.5.07, the respondents had informed the appellant/OP that they would not require room in a hotel as their invitees had made arrangement for the same and request was made for cancellation of room. It is also admitted position that the respondents/complainants had asked for refund of amount charged for room reservation but it was not agreed by the appellant/OP by stating that it was not possible as per agreed terms and conditions and further that the last minute cancellation was not possible.  The stand of the respondents/complainants is that when the appellant/OP declined to cancel the room, they had asked their invitees to use booked room for someone else. It is also the stand of respondents/complainants that since they had informed their invitees that they had the arrangement for accommodation, their invitees did not make arrangement of stay for them.  On reaching Munich, they found that appellant/OP had booked the rooms of respondents/complainants for someone else as a result of which they became helpless and homeless and had to make any of alternative arrangement by taking help of another company and were forced to pay extra amount of Rs.61,360/-.  The respondents/complainants had furnished proof in this regard i.e. receipt dated 28.7.07, Annexure-E and certificate issued by the company as Annexure-F.
12. The stand of the appellant is that they had agreed for cancellation of hotel accommodation booking and had also agreed to forego remaining Rs.10,000/- which was the balance amount to be paid by respondents/complainants.  However, there is no evidence to substantiate the same.  On one hand, the appellant/OP is alleging that they had refused to cancel as the same was not possible as per agreed terms and conditions.  On the other hand, it is alleged that as a special case, request of respondents/complainants was accepted.  There is no supporting evidence to prove the same.  Further the stand of the appellant/OP that they had agreed for providing hotel accommodation provided that an e-mail be sent by the agent of respondents/complainants and asked them to reach hotel is not believable.  Such a stand is taken to escape from the liability.  Had it informed so to respondents/complainants as is alleged, then why the respondents/complainants had to incur extra payment for making alternative arrangement as is established from evidence on record.
13. It is admitted position that the respondents/complainants when reached Munich found that appellant/OP had booked their rooms for someone else despite having paid for the said service.  One can imagine the plight of the person who is stranded at Airport in a foreign country without there being any hotel accommodation.  We find no infirmity in the findings given by the Ld. District Forum that there was deficiency on the part of appellant/OP in not providing hotel accommodation to the respondents/complainants which was booked for them. The Ld. District Forum after considering pleadings as well as evidence on record has given the said finding.
14.  No illegality or perversity is seen in the impugned order which calls for interference of this Commission.
15.  The appeal stands dismissed in limini.
16.  A copy of this order as per statutory requirements be forwarded to the parties free of charge and also to the concerned District Forum and thereafter the file be consigned to record room.
(Justice Veena Birbal)
